applicant_utility.summary: This fellowship only works if you already teach at a university in a developing country and do not hold a PhD - SNU screens explicitly for current employment in a recognised academic position. The package is strong: full tuition for six semesters, 1.5-2.0 million KRW a month for 3-4 years, economy round-trip airfare, evening Korean classes, health insurance and child care support, but only about 8 people win it per semester, so admission competitiveness is the real filter. There is no separate scholarship portal: the application rides on your SNU PhD admission application, which makes your admission dossier effectively your scholarship dossier.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Professors, lecturers, instructors and teaching or research assistants at universities in developing countries who hold a master's degree or higher and want a fully funded PhD at SNU.
application_readiness_checklist: Monitor the admissions notice page for the twice-yearly SPF announcement - rounds open with each international graduate admission cycle and the spring 2027 window was only four days long (6-9 July 2026)
Secure written proof of your current university employment naming your position and showing you teach an academic course or conduct academic research
Have your master's degree certificate from an accredited institution ready - expected master's holders need proof of at least six months of teaching/research employment
Prepare the full SNU PhD admission dossier in parallel, since admission documents and recommendation letters carry the scholarship review
Confirm the next round's exact dates by emailing intlscholarship@snu.ac.kr or calling +82-2-880-2519 (Office of Global Affairs)
common_rejection_risks: Forgetting the 'Application for Scholarship' checkbox - without it the application is assessed for admission only and the SPF is never considered

Failing to prove qualifying employment: roles outside the listed titles need certificate evidence they meet the teaching/research condition, and expected master's holders need six months of employment
Already holding a PhD, which disqualifies outright
Missing the short window because SPF deadlines are announced only days before they open
Not clearing the SNU admission stage first - SPF selection happens only after admission results
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The stipend is published as a range (KRW 1,500,000~2,000,000 per month) and the actual amount within it is not guaranteed; no housing or settling-in allowance is published, so recipients should budget for Seoul living costs beyond the stipend.
document_audit: Employment proof must show a listed title (Professor, Associate Professor, Assistant Professor, Research Professor, Lecturer, Instructor, Teaching Assistant, Research Assistant) - if your title differs, attach evidence your duties meet the teaching/research condition
Expected master's degree holders must document at least six months of employment teaching or conducting research
Use the application form attached to the current round's notice page - older forms may not match the current semester's requirements
alerts: The application window can be as short as four days (6-9 July 2026 for spring 2027), so check the notice page frequently once a round is rumoured
Airfare is economy class based on the GTS system and does not cover stopovers, upgrades or excess baggage
Insurance coverage and child care support amounts vary by recipient situation and are not guaranteed figures
SPF rounds recur every semester only alongside the international graduate admission cycle - if you miss the admission window, you miss the scholarship for that entry
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One-line: tick 'Application for Scholarship' inside the SNU PhD admission application, send evidential documents to the Office of Global Affairs, then wait for admission results, interview and decision.

benefits: Automatic entitlement: upon being selected for admission, the applicant is automatically entitled to the KAIST Scholarship

eligibility: Spring Semester, 2027 (Early only): candidates who have graduated or will graduate from his or her high school by February 28th, 2027
Fall Semester, 2027 (Early / Regular): candidates who have graduated or will graduate from his or her high school by August 31st, 2027
Applicants who hold Korean citizenship (dual citizenship) are not eligible to apply as foreign students

International applicants must additionally satisfy one of: neither of the applicant's parents is a Korean citizen, or, for applicants of Korean origin, the applicant received his or her entire elementary, junior high and high school education outside of Korea at a comparable and equivalent level (international schools located in Korea are NOT acknowledged as foreign schools)
Applicants who completed or will have completed high school in Korea are also welcomed to apply to the KAIST Undergraduate program
There is no transfer program for international students; applicants must apply as a freshman student
By the time of enrolment at KAIST the applicant must not hold any degree-seeking status from another university, otherwise admission shall be revoked

applicant_utility.summary: There is nothing to apply for separately: get admitted and this scholarship comes with it, so the only real task is winning the admission itself. What you get is full tuition for 8 semesters, 350,000 KRW a month and medical insurance - but KAIST's own budget table shows you still need about 3.36 million KRW a year (roughly 280,000 KRW a month) for housing, food and books, so treat this as partial funding, not full funding. The Early Admissions window for Spring 2027 closes 22 October 2026 at 6 PM KST, with the Regular Fall 2027 window closing 14 January 2027 - and you cannot switch tracks after paying the application fee.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International freshmen - including foreign nationals who finished high school in Korea - who want full tuition plus a monthly allowance without a separate scholarship form and can cover the remaining ~3.36 million KRW/year of living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Decide Early (Spring) vs Regular (Fall) before paying the application fee - after payment the track cannot be changed
Line up your recommendation letter early; it is due one week after the application deadline (29 October 2026 for Early, 21 January 2027 for Regular)
Do not forget to check 'KAIST scholarship' in the Statement of Financial Resources section of the online application
Budget for the uncovered costs KAIST itself lists - housing, food and books, about KRW 279,917 per month on the official cost table
Keep email access reliable after applying: only shortlisted applicants are contacted individually if an online interview is necessary
common_rejection_risks: Holding dual Korean citizenship, which blocks eligibility as a foreign student
Korean-origin applicants who studied at an international school inside Korea - those schools are not acknowledged as foreign schools
Missing the high-school graduation cut-off: 28 February 2027 for Spring entry, 31 August 2027 for Fall entry
Holding any degree-seeking status at another university at enrolment, which revokes admission
A late recommendation letter - the later letter deadline is final and separate from the application deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: KAIST's official cost table puts the essential annual budget at KRW 14,885,680 and the scholarship offset at KRW 11,738,360, leaving KRW 3,359,000 per year (KRW 1,679,500 per semester, about KRW 279,917 per month) for housing, food and books that the student must fund.
